passage:
Hansa was twenty-two when Samir began writing to her from breakfast until midnight. "You are my destiny." "I have never met anyone like you." "Cancel your plans, I want you all to myself." Nobody had ever made her feel so seen, and within three weeks she had stopped answering her friends' calls.

By the time she turned twenty-three, the messages had thinned to one-line replies. When she mentioned a work dinner, Samir wrote, "You always make everything about yourself." Hansa rehearsed apologies, cooked his favourite food and kept her phone beside her plate, trying to win back the warmth of those first weeks.

Her friend Anjali found her crying in the stairwell. "The person who wrote all those words in week one is not the person you're chasing now," Anjali said quietly. "Come and stay with me tonight." Hansa nodded. The next morning, over tea, she opened her phone and typed a message to her sister instead of Samir.

qa.q: What did Samir write to Hansa in the first weeks?
qa.a: He wrote that she was his destiny, that he had never met anyone like her, and asked her to cancel her plans.

qa.q: How do the first weeks with Samir differ from the time after Hansa turned twenty-three?
qa.a: At first the constant messages and declarations made Hansa feel seen, leaving little room to learn who Samir really was; later he sent one-line replies and criticism while she worked to win back the early warmth, and the gap between the two phases is the pattern.

qa.q: What was Hansa feeling as she cooked his favourite food and kept her phone beside her plate?
qa.a: Hansa felt anxious and eager to earn back the closeness she had lost, working hard to please him.

qa.q: How did Anjali's response help Hansa?
qa.a: Anjali stayed with her, named the gap between the early words and the current behaviour, and offered a safe place to stay that night, which gave Hansa room to reach out to her sister.

grounding: Love-bombing shown in two phases: the flood of early declarations that sweeps a young adult up, and the later cold shift that leaves her working to earn the warmth back.
